'''Mirosław Sawicki''' (February 10, 1946, Warsaw — January 31, 2016)<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2016-02-01|date=1 February 2016|title=Żegnamy Mirka Sawickiego|url=http://www.otwarta.org/zegnamy-mirka-sawickiego/|website=otwarta.org}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> was a <ref>{{Cite web |title=Mirosław Sawicki spoczął na warszawskich Powązkach |url=https://dzieje.pl/aktualnosci/miroslaw-sawicki-spoczal-na-warszawskich-powazkach |access-date=2023-09-28 |website=dzieje.pl |language=pl}}</ref>[[physics teacher]], activist and civil servant. The former director of the central examination commission was also the [[Ministry of National Education (Poland)#Ministers of National Education and Sport|Minister of National Education and Sports]] in 2004–2005,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mirosław Sawicki spoczął na warszawskich Powązkach |url=https://dzieje.pl/aktualnosci/miroslaw-sawicki-spoczal-na-warszawskich-powazkach |access-date=2023-09-28 |website=dzieje.pl |language=pl}}</ref> and [[Ministry of National Education (Poland)#Ministers of National Education|Minister of National Education]] in 2005.

== Biography ==
Beginning in 1954, he was active in the [[Polish Scouting and Guiding Association|scouting movement]] as part of [[Jacek Kuroń]]'s Walter Hufz. He attended the Tadeusz Reytan High School VI in [[Warsaw]]. In 1963, he began studying at the Faculty of Physics at [[University of Warsaw]].<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2020-11-18|date=10 June 2005|title=Wiekowe liceum|url=https://wiadomosci.wp.pl/wiekowe-liceum-6036371449083009a|website=wp.pl|archive-url=https://archive.today/20201115041413/https://wiadomosci.wp.pl/wiekowe-liceum-6036371449083009a|archive-date=2020-11-15}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> In 1968, as part of the [[1968 Polish political crisis|March events]], he took part in a rally at the University of Warsaw in defence of the play ''[[Dziady (poem)|Dziady]]'' and [[Adam Michnik]] and [[Henryk Szlajfer]], who had been expelled from the university. During this time he was associated with the so-called [[banana youth]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bromber |first1=Emilia |title="To nie my, to oni". Marzec 1968 |url=https://fwpn.org.pl/mloda-redakcja/mloda-redakcja-2018/-to-nie-my-to-oni-marzec-1968-Y5NUaz |website=fwpn.org.pl |publisher=[[Foundation for German-Polish Cooperation]] |language=Pl |date=2018}}</ref> At that time he was suspended as a student, which was reinstated in 1970. In 1971 he received his bachelor's degree, and received his master's degree from the [[University of Białystok|Bialystok]] branch of the University of Warsaw in 1982.

From 1971 to 1990, he was employed as a teacher of physics in Warsaw high schools, including XLI Joachim Lelewel High School. In the second half of the 1970s, he collaborated with the [[KOR Committee for Social Self-Defense|Committee for Social Self-Defense KOR]]. In 1980, he joined the Independent Self-Governing Trade Union [[Solidarity (Polish trade union)|Solidarity]], where he headed teams dealing with education. In 1989, he headed the [[Solidarity Citizens' Committee]] of [[Śródmieście, Warsaw]].

From 1990 to 1997 he was an official at the [[Ministry of National Education (Poland)|Ministry of National Education]], serving as director of the Department of General Education (until 1996), then as undersecretary of state at the ministry. From 1998 to 2002 he held the position of Minister Counselor at the [[Embassy of Poland, Washington, D.C.|Polish Embassy in Washington]].

In 2002, he opened his doctoral dissertation at the Department of Sociology at [[Jagiellonian University]]. In the same year he won a competition for the post of director of the Central Examination Commission (CKE). On May 2, 2004, he became Minister of National Education and Sports in [[First Cabinet of Marek Belka|Marek Belka's first government]], a position he retained in the next cabinet. After the separation of the sports ministry, he was Minister of National Education from September 1, 2005, to October 31, 2005. He then returned to heading the CKE, a position he was dismissed from in March 2006. In 2008 he became a member of the National Education Council, an advisory body to Minister [[Katarzyna Hall]]. In the same year, he again headed the CKE (as acting director), serving in this position until January 2009, later becoming deputy director of the institution. He was also a member of the Association of Employees, Collaborators and Friends of the Polish Radio Free Europe Broadcasting Station named after Jan Nowak-Jezioranski.

The son of Ludwik and Czesława ({{nee}} Żochowska). He was the husband of Paula Sawicka.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2022-02-27|author=Joanna Derda|date=11 December 2012|title=Paula Sawicka: Lekcje tolerancji|url=http://zwierciadlo.pl/2012/kultura/kultura-wywiady/paula-sawicka-lekcje-tolerancji/attachment/paula-sawicka|website=zwierciadlo.pl |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150427144357/http://zwierciadlo.pl/2012/kultura/kultura-wywiady/paula-sawicka-lekcje-tolerancji/attachment/paula-sawicka |archive-date=27 April 2015 }}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

He was buried in the [[Powązki Military Cemetery]] (cemetery section B32-20-5).<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2020-03-08|title=Wyszukiwarka cmentarna – Warszawskie cmentarze|url=http://www.cmentarzekomunalne.com.pl/mapa/mapa.php?cment=PWZKI&rzad=20&kwatera=B%2032&grob=5&dane=+imie=mir+nazwisko=Sawicki+check_nazwisko=on+check_ur=+rok=1800+miesiac=1+dzien=1+rok2=2020+miesiac2=3+dzien2=8+check_zg=+rok_zg1=1800+miesiac_zg1=1+dzien_zg1=1+rok_zg2=2020+miesiac_zg2=3+dzien_zg2=8+cmentarz=powazkowski#kotwica|website=cmentarzekomunalne.com.pl}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>
